sheets.title: DEEP SPACE 1
sheets.purpose: NASA / JPL · 1998–2001. Explore the spacecraft, then follow energy, xenon, observations and commands. Functional arrangement; geometry is not to scale.

parts.label: SUN
parts.what: Incident solar radiation supplies the electrical energy used by the spacecraft.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32

parts.label: ELECTRICAL POWER
parts.what: SCARLET concentrator arrays, battery and power distribution supply the spacecraft and its ion propulsion system.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32

parts.label: ION PROPULSION
parts.what: A single NSTAR xenon ion thruster provides sustained interplanetary acceleration.
refs: Rayman et al., DS1 primary mission results, 1999
NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32

parts.label: NAVIGATION AND ATTITUDE
parts.what: AutoNav estimates the trajectory; attitude control points the vehicle, using sensors, hydrazine thrusters and the ion-engine gimbal.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32

parts.label: INSTRUMENTS
parts.what: MICAS collects images and spectra; PEPE measures charged particles. MICAS also supplies optical navigation observations.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32

parts.label: AVIONICS
parts.what: The integrated electronics module houses most spacecraft electronics and supports command execution, software and data handling.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32
parts.note: Software boxes elsewhere in this drawing are logical functions, not separate flight computers.

parts.label: RADIO SYSTEM
parts.what: The small deep-space transponder connects onboard data handling to X-band and Ka-band radio hardware.

parts.label: GROUND
parts.what: Earth stations receive telemetry and radiometric observations and send spacecraft commands.

parts.label: AUTONOMY SOFTWARE
parts.what: Remote Agent and Beacon Monitor demonstrated onboard planning, execution, diagnosis and compact health reporting.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32
parts.note: Remote Agent and Beacon Monitor were experiments, not continuous replacements for the operations team.

parts.label: STRUCTURE
parts.what: An aluminum bus supports the flight hardware; insulation, heaters and radiators regulate temperature.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32

steps.text: Illustrative energy path: sunlight reaches the deployed solar wings.
SCARLET concentrates light onto photovoltaic cells.
Electrical power is shared between flight equipment and propulsion.
The propulsion power processor supplies the engine electrical loads.
Accelerated xenon carries momentum away and changes the spacecraft trajectory. Open this sheet for the propellant and engine detail.
Illustrative data path: MICAS or PEPE acquires an observation.
The observation enters spacecraft data handling.
Telemetry is delivered to the small deep-space transponder.
The selected antenna transmits the encoded signal to Earth.
The Deep Space Network delivers the received data for mission processing.

sheets.title: ELECTRICAL POWER
sheets.purpose: Two four-panel SCARLET wings supply about 2.5 kW at 1 AU. A nickel-hydrogen battery supports deployment and transient loads.

parts.label: SUNLIGHT
parts.what: Sunlight is the input to the concentrator array.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32

parts.label: FRESNEL LENSES
parts.what: Cylindrical silicone Fresnel lenses concentrate light onto narrow solar-cell strips.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32

parts.label: SOLAR CELLS
parts.what: Photovoltaic cells convert the concentrated radiation to electrical power.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32
parts.note: Output varies with solar distance, orientation and aging. The solar-array figure is not power delivered entirely to propulsion.

parts.label: ARRAY GIMBALS
parts.what: A single-axis gimbal on each wing controls pointing along the more sensitive array axis.
refs: Rayman et al., DS1 primary mission results, 1999
parts.why: Concentrating optics require controlled solar illumination.

parts.label: POWER DISTRIBUTION
parts.what: Power conditioning and distribution deliver electrical power to the spacecraft loads.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32

parts.label: BATTERY
parts.what: Nickel-hydrogen storage powers the spacecraft before array deployment and supplements the arrays during load transients or unfavorable pointing.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32

parts.label: FLIGHT EQUIPMENT
parts.what: Flight electronics, instruments, telecommunications and heaters draw from the spacecraft electrical system.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32

parts.label: PROPULSION POWER
parts.what: The propulsion power processing unit converts its input into the electrical supplies required by the ion engine.
refs: Rayman et al., DS1 primary mission results, 1999
NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32

parts.label: SWITCH EXPERIMENT
parts.what: The Power Actuation and Switching Module demonstrated voltage/current sensing and current limiting.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32
parts.note: Shown as a technology experiment; it is not asserted to be the sole power switch for every flight load.

steps.text: Illustrative energy path through the deployed array.
Incoming rays enter the cylindrical concentrator lenses.
The lenses focus the light onto photovoltaic strips.
The electrical output reaches power conditioning and distribution.
Available propulsion power is allocated after spacecraft needs are met.
The power processor supplies the ion engine. Its operating point depends on the available power.

sheets.title: ION PROPULSION
sheets.purpose: NSTAR uses electrical energy to accelerate xenon. Propellant feed, power processing and control are distinct functions.

parts.label: XENON STORAGE
parts.what: The xenon supply provides reaction mass for the ion propulsion system.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32

parts.label: XENON FEED
parts.what: The feed system regulates xenon delivery to the engine discharge chamber and cathodes.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32

parts.label: NSTAR THRUSTER
parts.what: A discharge ionizes xenon; electrostatic grids accelerate the ions; a separate cathode neutralizes the exiting beam.
refs: Rayman et al., DS1 primary mission results, 1999
NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32
parts.note: These are design endpoints reported in the primary-mission paper. They are not a claim that maximum thrust was sustained throughout the flight.

parts.label: EXHAUST
parts.what: The outgoing xenon beam carries momentum; its reaction accelerates the spacecraft.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32

parts.label: ENGINE CONTROL
parts.what: The ion-engine controller sequences starts, operating settings and shutdowns under spacecraft commands.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32

parts.label: POWER PROCESSOR
parts.what: The PPU supplies the electrical operating conditions for the discharge, cathodes and ion optics.
refs: Rayman et al., DS1 primary mission results, 1999
NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32

parts.label: THRUSTER GIMBAL
parts.what: Two-axis gimbaling steers the thrust vector and supplies attitude-control torque while thrusting.
parts.note: The gimbal does not provide all three attitude-control axes; hydrazine is still needed.

parts.label: PLUME DIAGNOSTICS
parts.what: Ion Propulsion System Diagnostic Subsystem sensors observe plume interactions with the spacecraft.
refs: Rayman et al., DS1 primary mission results, 1999
NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32
parts.why: Tests address contamination, erosion and the compatibility of electric propulsion with instruments.

steps.text: Illustrative propellant path for a normal ion-engine operating interval.
Xenon leaves storage through the feed system.
Regulation and metering establish the required flows.
Gas enters the discharge and cathode systems.
Electron impact creates positive xenon ions; the grids extract and accelerate them.
Xenon exits in a beam neutralized by electrons from the neutralizer.
Continuous low thrust accumulates velocity change over long operating periods.

sheets.title: NSTAR ENGINE MECHANISM
sheets.purpose: Schematic physical mechanism, not an assembly section. The discharge cathode and beam neutralizer perform different jobs.

parts.label: NEUTRAL XENON
parts.what: Neutral xenon atoms enter the engine from the metered feed system.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32

parts.label: DISCHARGE CHAMBER
parts.what: Energetic electrons collide with xenon atoms, producing positive xenon ions and additional electrons in the discharge plasma.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32

parts.label: ION OPTICS
parts.what: A pair of perforated molybdenum grids establishes the electric field that extracts and accelerates positive xenon ions.
refs: Rayman et al., DS1 primary mission results, 1999
NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32

parts.label: OUTGOING BEAM
parts.what: Fast xenon ions carry momentum away from the thruster.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32

parts.label: DISCHARGE CATHODE
parts.what: This hollow cathode emits the electrons that sustain ionization inside the discharge chamber.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32

parts.label: MAGNETIC CONFINEMENT
parts.what: Magnets prolong electron residence in the discharge, increasing the opportunity for ionizing collisions.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32

parts.label: POWER SUPPLIES
parts.what: The external power processor establishes the discharge and grid potentials and powers the cathode circuits.
refs: Rayman et al., DS1 primary mission results, 1999
NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32

parts.label: NEUTRALIZER CATHODE
parts.what: A separate cathode emits electrons into the exiting ion beam to balance charge and prevent excessive spacecraft charging.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32
parts.why: Momentum transfer comes from accelerated xenon; the neutralizer maintains charge balance.
parts.note: Beam neutralization does not require every xenon ion to recombine into an individual neutral atom.

steps.text: Illustrative particle path, with geometry simplified for explanation.
A neutral xenon atom enters the discharge chamber.
An energetic electron removes an atomic electron; the xenon becomes a positive ion.
The ion reaches the extraction region.
The electric field accelerates it outward through the aligned grid apertures.
A separate electron population supplied by the neutralizer balances the beam charge.

sheets.title: NAVIGATION AND ATTITUDE
sheets.purpose: AutoNav estimates where the spacecraft is going; attitude control points it. The dashed camera path identifies the 2000 recovery configuration.

parts.label: MICAS IMAGES
parts.what: The visible camera supplies images of reference asteroids and background stars for optical navigation.
refs: Rayman et al., DS1 primary mission results, 1999

parts.label: AUTONAV
parts.what: Onboard image processing and orbit determination estimate the trajectory; maneuver planning computes corrections.
refs: Rayman et al., DS1 primary mission results, 1999
parts.note: AutoNav is distinct from the attitude controller and the Remote Agent experiment.

parts.label: MANEUVER COMMANDS
parts.what: Required maneuvers become pointing and propulsion requests subject to spacecraft constraints.
refs: Rayman et al., DS1 primary mission results, 1999

parts.label: STAR TRACKER
parts.what: The stellar reference unit normally measured orientation from stars.
parts.note: V means the historical fact is verified, not that this unit remained operational. It failed during the extended mission.

parts.label: INERTIAL UNIT
parts.what: Gyroscope measurements support attitude propagation between optical references.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32

parts.label: ATTITUDE CONTROL
parts.what: The attitude-control software combines measurements with pointing requests and commands the actuators.

parts.label: SUN SENSOR
parts.what: Sun sensing supports solar orientation and safe attitude operation.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32

parts.label: HYDRAZINE SYSTEM
parts.what: Chemical thrusters provide attitude-control torques and can make trajectory corrections.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32
Rayman et al., DS1 primary mission results, 1999

parts.label: ION-ENGINE GIMBAL
parts.what: Thrust-vector steering provides control about two axes while the ion engine is operating.

steps.text: Illustrative AutoNav path: the visible camera images a reference asteroid against cataloged stars.
Measured directions enter onboard navigation.
The navigation solution is used to plan a trajectory correction.
The attitude controller receives the required pointing request.
During ion thrusting, the controller steers the thrust vector.
The engine delivers thrust in the commanded direction; this sheet isolates pointing from the separate engine-start sequence.
Illustrative recovery path, based on the June 2000 return to controlled flight after the November 1999 star-tracker failure.
Revised software uses MICAS star observations as an attitude reference.
The recovery combines intermittent camera references with inertial measurements; it does not restore the failed hardware.
The controller commands chemical thrusters when attitude correction requires them.
The recovered pointing capability supports resumed operations and the later Borrelly encounter.

sheets.title: SCIENCE INSTRUMENTS
sheets.purpose: MICAS shares one telescope across four channels. PEPE separately measures plasma. The ultraviolet channel was flown but did not produce usable science.

parts.label: LIGHT
parts.what: Reflected or emitted light from targets enters MICAS. The mission observed asteroid Braille and comet Borrelly.

parts.label: OPTICS
parts.what: A common silicon-carbide optical assembly serves two visible cameras and ultraviolet and infrared spectrometers.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32

parts.label: VISIBLE CCD
parts.what: The CCD channel supplies visible images for science and optical navigation; later it also provides star observations for attitude recovery.
refs: Rayman et al., DS1 primary mission results, 1999

parts.label: ACTIVE PIXEL SENSOR
parts.what: A second visible imager demonstrates integration of detector and support electronics.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32
Rayman et al., DS1 primary mission results, 1999

parts.label: INFRARED SPECTROMETER
parts.what: The infrared channel measures spectral information used to investigate target composition. Spacecraft motion supplies the push-broom scan.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32

parts.label: ULTRAVIOLET CHANNEL
parts.what: The ultraviolet imaging spectrometer was installed, but its detector chain did not return interpretable data.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32
parts.note: The dashed output denotes the unavailable science path. Verified status describes this documented outcome.

parts.label: INSTRUMENT DATA
parts.what: Image, spectrum and particle measurements enter onboard data handling for processing and transmission.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32

parts.label: PLASMA
parts.what: Solar-wind and encounter particles are the input to PEPE; the engine plume can also affect the local environment.
refs: Rayman et al., DS1 primary mission results, 1999
NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32

parts.label: PEPE
parts.what: The Plasma Experiment for Planetary Exploration measures electron/ion energies and ion mass-to-charge, and examines propulsion-plasma interactions.
refs: Rayman et al., DS1 primary mission results, 1999
NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32

steps.text: Illustrative optical path: target light reaches MICAS.
The shared telescope collects the light.
The visible CCD forms a two-dimensional image.
CCD images support science and optical navigation; the same channel later supports attitude recovery.
The image enters onboard processing and telemetry.
Observations are returned through the spacecraft radio system.
Illustrative particle path: ambient ions and electrons reach the instrument.
PEPE admits and analyzes the charged-particle population.
The instrument measures energies and ion mass-to-charge, including evidence of the local xenon environment.
Particle measurements are delivered to spacecraft data handling.
These observations complement the remote-sensing data from MICAS.

sheets.title: TELECOMMUNICATIONS
sheets.purpose: X-band carries commands and telemetry. Ka-band supplies an additional experimental downlink. Antennas are fixed to the spacecraft.

parts.label: TELEMETRY INPUT
parts.what: The integrated electronics module supplies the telemetry bitstream and clock to the radio.

parts.label: SMALL TRANSPONDER
parts.what: SDST combines command reception, telemetry modulation and X-/Ka-band excitation. Detected commands return to flight electronics.

parts.label: X-BAND AMPLIFIER
parts.what: The solid-state X-band amplifier raises downlink RF power.

parts.label: KA-BAND AMPLIFIER
parts.what: The KaPA amplifies the Ka-band exciter output.
parts.note: 2.2 W is the in-flight value in the 2001 telecommunications report; an earlier report quotes 2.3 W.

parts.label: X-BAND ANTENNAS
parts.what: Switches select the high-gain antenna, +X low-gain antenna, or coupled +Z/−Z low-gain pair for uplink and downlink.
parts.note: The HGA and +X LGA point along +X. The other LGAs point along +Z and −Z. Antenna pointing requires turning the spacecraft.

parts.label: KA-BAND HORN
parts.what: The fixed Ka-band horn points along +X and radiates the additional downlink.

parts.label: DSN STATIONS
parts.what: Earth stations receive spacecraft signals. DS1 Ka-band tests used Goldstone facilities.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32

parts.label: COMMAND OUTPUT
parts.what: Recovered command bits are delivered to the integrated electronics module for decoding and execution.

steps.text: Illustrative Ka-band telemetry path.
The electronics module supplies telemetry bits and timing.
The Ka-band exciter produces a modulated radio signal.
KaPA supplies RF power to the fixed horn.
The signal travels to the receiving station on Earth.
The ground system receives and decodes the telemetry.
Illustrative command path: an Earth station transmits at X-band.
The signal reaches the selected X-band antenna configuration.
The receiver detects the uplink and recovers command bits.
The radio supplies recovered bits to spacecraft command handling.
Flight electronics decode and execute the command. There is no Ka-band command uplink on DS1.

sheets.title: AUTONOMY EXPERIMENTS
sheets.purpose: Software functions share onboard computing. Remote Agent ran selected May 1999 tests; Beacon Monitor was a separate technology experiment.

parts.label: GOALS
parts.what: Operators supply high-level objectives and constraints for the Remote Agent experiment.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32
JPL Remote Agent flight announcement, May 17, 1999

parts.label: PLANNER
parts.what: The planner constructs activities and timing relationships that satisfy the supplied goals and resource constraints.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32
JPL Remote Agent flight announcement, May 17, 1999

parts.label: EXECUTIVE
parts.what: The executive expands planned activities into subsystem commands and monitors their execution.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32
JPL Remote Agent flight announcement, May 17, 1999

parts.label: FLIGHT SUBSYSTEMS
parts.what: The experiment commands selected real flight systems, including ion propulsion, while monitoring their responses.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32
JPL Remote Agent flight announcement, May 17, 1999

parts.label: LIVINGSTONE
parts.what: Model-based state estimation and recovery identify operating modes and help select recovery actions.
refs: JPL Remote Agent flight announcement, May 17, 1999

parts.label: ENGINEERING DATA
parts.what: Subsystem telemetry provides evidence of state, performance and possible anomalies.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32

parts.label: BEACON MONITOR
parts.what: Health summarization maps the spacecraft condition to one of four assistance states.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32
Rayman et al., DS1 primary mission results, 1999

parts.label: RADIO BEACON
parts.what: SDST can transmit a tone representing the requested degree of ground attention.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32
Rayman et al., DS1 primary mission results, 1999
parts.note: Tested during selected periods; DS1 did not dispense with routine mission operations or normal telemetry.

steps.text: Illustrative Remote Agent command path during an enabled test period.
A high-level objective reaches the planning system.
The resulting plan specifies activities and constraints.
The executive issues commands to selected flight subsystems.
Telemetry reports the resulting hardware state.
State estimation checks observations against the system model.
Diagnosis and recovery information guide subsequent execution.
The first May 1999 test encountered an executive software fault; a follow-up test completed the remaining objectives.
Illustrative Beacon Monitor path, separate from the Remote Agent planner.
Engineering measurements are summarized against activity-dependent limits.
The summary indicates whether no help, convenient contact, prompt contact or urgent assistance is needed.
The selected state determines the radio tone.
Ground monitors detect the tone and can arrange fuller tracking and telemetry.

sheets.title: STRUCTURE AND THERMAL
sheets.purpose: The physical bus supports externally mounted equipment. This sheet records the documented envelope, thermal measures and structural experiment.

parts.label: EQUIPMENT
parts.what: Most components mount outside the central bus for accessible integration and replacement before launch.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32

parts.label: PRIMARY BUS
parts.what: The primary spacecraft bus carries structural loads and supports the mounted subsystems.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32
parts.note: Dimensions are the July 1999 NASA press-kit envelope. Drawing solids are symbolic, with no dimensional scale.

parts.label: LAUNCH INTERFACE
parts.what: The launch adapter and propulsion module form the lower spacecraft assembly identified in the NASA configuration drawing.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32

parts.label: THERMAL BLANKETS
parts.what: Multilayer insulation reduces unwanted radiative heat exchange.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32

parts.label: ELECTRICAL HEATERS
parts.what: Powered heaters help maintain equipment within allowable temperature ranges.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32

parts.label: RADIATORS
parts.what: Radiating surfaces dispose of heat to space.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32

parts.label: MULTIFUNCTIONAL PANEL
parts.what: A composite test panel combines load-bearing structure, copper-polyimide electrical interconnects, embedded heat transfer and an external radiating surface.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32

parts.label: LOW-POWER ELECTRONICS
parts.what: Experimental low-voltage devices and architectures investigate reduced electronics power consumption.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32
parts.note: This separate experiment belongs to the twelve-technology payload. It is intentionally unconnected here: the consulted sources do not establish a specific interface to the multifunctional panel. Experimental devices did not replace every spacecraft circuit.

parts.label: SERVICE BOOM
parts.what: The boom provides access to battery and propellant service connections inside the launch fairing; it also carries the −Z low-gain antenna.
refs: NASA DS1 press kit, July 1999, pp. 7, 19–32

steps.text: Illustrative structural load path; attachment geometry is schematic.
Mounted equipment transfers mechanical load to the aluminum bus.
The primary structure distributes the load.
The load continues through the launch-interface structure.
This path matters while the spacecraft is attached to the launcher. The interface remains part of the flight assembly after separation.

blocks.p: A source-grounded functional drawing set of NASA Deep Space 1, prepared 27 October 2026. It covers major hardware and all twelve technology demonstrations. External inputs and ground systems are included where they explain a connection.

blocks.note: Positions, solid shapes and connecting lines are schematic. This is not a dimensioned fabrication drawing, a verified harness diagram or a literal three-dimensional spacecraft reconstruction. V means the component or historical statement is documented; it does not mean every flight unit remained operational.

blocks.p: Each trace illustrates a documented mechanism or operating path. None is a reconstructed time series from flight telemetry. Links between structural parts denote mechanical or thermal relationships, as labeled, rather than data flow.

For physical mounting locations, see the [original NASA two-view configuration plate, printed p. 32 / PDF p. 34](https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/news/press_kits/ds1asteroid.pdf#page=34). The plate shows the arrays stowed; the deployed span is supplied separately in the specifications.

kv: 29 July 1999 UTC (28 July in U.S. Pacific time)

blocks.p: Historical dates follow [NASA mission history](https://science.nasa.gov/mission/deep-space-1/) and the [JPL navigation engineering report](https://descanso.jpl.nasa.gov/DPSummary/DS1_Navigation_rev.pdf). Launch-era publications contain planned events; plans are not treated as completed outcomes.

list: 1. Solar electric propulsion — ion propulsion and NSTAR mechanism sheets.

blocks.p: NASA lists these in the [July 1999 press kit](https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/news/press_kits/ds1asteroid.pdf). Ordinary hardware such as the star tracker and nickel-hydrogen battery was also essential to the spacecraft.

list: [Rayman et al., DS1 primary mission results, 1999](https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/nmp/ds1/DS1_Primary_Mission.pdf)

blocks.note: The press kit establishes hardware and design intent. Later engineering reports and mission history establish in-flight outcomes. Performance figures retain their operating condition; max design thrust, array output and PPU input are different quantities.

list: Click a subsystem to open its sheet. Click an ordinary part to read function, specifications, caveats and source links.
Drag empty space to orbit; shift-drag to pan; scroll to zoom. ISO, TOP, FRONT and FIT control the view.
Drag a component to rearrange the schematic; double-click restores its position.
TRACE buttons step through the operating paths. Arrow keys move between steps.
Use the breadcrumb or Escape to return. INDEX lists the parts on a sheet.
Dashed links identify feedback, recovery or unavailable paths; each link label specifies its meaning.
